subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Password Hygiene That Works
description: A 60-second lesson on Password Hygiene That Works.

hook.text: The most common password in the world is still '123456.' It protects millions of accounts.

buildup.text: Password managers generate and store unique passwords for every site you use.

discovery.text: A unique password per site means one breach can never cascade to your other accounts.

twist.text: Two-factor authentication adds a second barrier — even if your password is stolen.

climax.text: Most account takeovers succeed because of reused passwords, not sophisticated hacking.

punchline.text: A password manager costs $3 a month. A breach costs thousands.

quiz.question: Why do password managers protect against identity theft?
options: They create unique passwords so one breach can't cascade
